question.leadin: This city-state's agoge [uh-goh-gay] system trained young men for battle and inclusion in society; the training was successful enough that this city-state went without walls.
question.text: Name this highly militaristic ancient Greek city-state that lost 300 warriors in a mountain pass at Thermopylae in 480 BCE.
question.clue: Every autumn, this city redeclared war on the enslaved helots.

swap.leadin: Xerxes burned this city during his invasion of the Greek peninsula.
swap.text: Name this democratic city-state whose rulers included Solon, and whose Acropolis contains the Parthenon.
swap.clue: A bema, or speaker's platform, lies on this city's Pnyx hill.

question.leadin: The introduction of the sarissa pike by this country's Philip II revolutionized its military.
question.text: Name this ancient country that gained control of Greece after winning at Chaeronea. A modern country of this name has capital at Skopje.
question.answerHtml: Macedonia [accept Macedon, prompt “Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia” or “Fyrom” ]
question.clue: This kingdom, which was annexed by Rome after the Battle of Pydna, formed a federation of Greek cities called the League of Corinth after it defeated Thebes at the Battle of Chaeronea.

swap.leadin: Give the following about the aftermath of the 405 BCE Battle of Aegospotami [ay- gus-pah-tuh-mee].
swap.text: At Aegospotami, Lysander led a rout of the Athenian navy, thus essentially ending this war over control of the Greek mainland.
swap.clue: A history of this conflict records emissaries saying "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must" before killing and enslaving the population of Melos.

question.leadin: This man opposed Nicias and led Athens on the disastrous Sicilian Expedition.
question.text: Name this general, whose constantly shifting loyalties caused him to defect to Sparta and then defect to the court of the Persian satrap Tissaphernes.
question.clue: This person organized the 411 BC coup that installed the Four Hundred before being defeated by Lysander at the battle of Notium.

swap.leadin: Identify these other rulers of Athens.
swap.text: The son of Megacles, this man reformed the constitution of ancient Athens and set the city on a democratic footing. For these accomplishments he became known as "the father of Athenian democracy."
swap.clue: He increased the size of the Boule to five hundred and the number of tribes from four to ten.

question.text: This Greek city on an isthmus had an ancient greased track called the diolkos replaced with a canal in the 19th century.
question.clue: According to Herodotus, this city provided 40 ships at the Battle of Salamis, the second most after Athens.

swap.leadin: His only surviving work is divided into sections titled after muses, and is structured around the rule of four Persian emperors.
swap.text: Name this Greek "Father of History" who chronicled the Greco-Persian Wars.
swap.clue: This author likely confused marmots for giant gold-digging ants in India.

question.leadin: This period marks the second of three devised by Christian Jurgensen Thomsen.
question.text: Name this period of human history, during which England's Wessex culture developed and the Minoan civilization flourished. The Greek Dark Ages began after the collapse of the civilizations from this period.
question.clue: Earlier in this time period, Greece had been home to the Minoans.

swap.text: The Bronze Age Collapse ended the use of this written script, the only one in the Mycenaean language that has been deciphered.
swap.clue: This system consists of ninety syllabic signs, all of which correspond to open syllables.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the early Dark Ages.
question.text: Historians look at the "migration" of people known by this term, which included the Huns and Ostrogoths. The Romans used this term to refer to the "uncivilized" tribes of people living outside their borders.
question.clue: A word that is probably derived from the Greek word rha plus the Greek root of this word is traditionally used by stage actors to imitate the sound of indistinct conversation.

swap.leadin: Name these leagues of Greek city-states.
swap.text: Originally created in opposition to Macedonian rule of Greece, this league of city-states named after a northern region of the Peloponnese was eventually conquered by Rome, and counted Philopoemen and Polybius among its members.
swap.clue: A brief war named for this power took place after the Romans defeated Andriscus in the Fourth Macedonian War.

question.leadin: After he was tried for failing to capture this city, one monarch explained that because he had really captured a nearby forest of the same name, he had fulfilled an oracle's prophecy.
question.text: Name this city that was the origin and namesake of the Macedonian royal family. This city engaged in the Battle of the Champions with its longtime rival, Sparta.
question.clue: This city's Hybristica ("hye-BRIS-tick-uh") festival has been linked to its supposed defence after the Battle of Sepeia ("SEH-pay-ah") by the female poet Telesilla.

swap.text: In the 220s BCE-era Cleomenean War, the Achaean League fought Sparta and this allied polis that expanded into perioikic Margana and Amphidolis. Circa 400 BCE, Sparta fought this polis for banning it from a temple of Zeus.
swap.answerHtml: Elis [or Ilia or Eleia or Elida; prompt on, but do not otherwise reveal, Olympiá by asking “what polis was that sanctuary controlled by?”]
swap.clue: This city constructed its Prytaneion near the Pelopion in one sanctuary during the sixth century BC in order to emphasise this polis' control over it.

question.leadin: This unit fought at the extreme left wing of the victorious side at the Battle of Leuctra.
question.text: Name this elite fighting whose members are commemorate by a stone lion at the site of their destruction during the Battle of Chaeronea. It was composed of 150 pairs of lovers.
question.answerHtml: Sacred Band of Thebes [or Hieros Lokhos; do not accept answers with “Carthage” since that’s a completely different group]
question.clue: This group played a major role in winning a decisive victory at the Battle of Leuctra.

swap.leadin: The Ptolemaic, Seleucid, and Antigonid dynasties all arose during this era.
swap.text: Name this term from classical history for the era in which Greek culture flourished across Eurasia and Africa in the wake of Alexander the Great's conquests.
swap.clue: Another sculpture from this period was attributed by Pliny the Elder to Athanodoros, Hagesandros, and Polydoros of Rhodes, although he inaccurately claims that it was made from one block of marble.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the so-called "Athenian Empire,"
question.text: The "Athenian Empire" mainly grew out of the possessions of a "League" centered on this Aegean island. The 454 B.C. transfer of the League's treasury from this island to Athens symbolized Athens' growing imperialism.
question.clue: Dying in this location was prohibited in a ritual purification during the Peloponnesian War.

swap.leadin: The final city usually included in this group became the site of the Italiote League, which was eventually destroyed at the Battle of the Elleporus.
swap.text: Give this term which refers to a group of colonies along the coast of southern Italy, starting with the Euboean colonies of Cumae and Pithecusae around 750 BC and ending with Heraclea circa 433 BC.
swap.clue: Tarquin the Proud died in exile in a city in this region.

question.leadin: This event was sparked by the execution of Agathocles and opened the door for the Gallic invasion of Greece, as the Macedonian hold on the Balkans became untenable. FTPE.
question.text: Name this 281 BCE battle, sometimes called the last of the wars of the Diadochi, at which Lysimachus was killed by the forces of Seleucus Nicator.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the three kings named Antigonus.
swap.text: Antigonus I, also known as the One-Eyed was a participant in these conflicts so-named after the "great funeral games" after the death of Alexander the Great. They include the Lamian War, and other participants in this conflict include the namesake of the Seleucid Dynasty.
swap.clue: This military conflict from the end of the fourth century BCE, in which Alexander the Great's successors fought over the remnants of his empire at such places as Ipsus.
